newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Chronology of Afghanistan's 24 years of turmoil.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of Afghanistan's 24 years of turmoil.

text.p: The capture of opposition strongholds by the Taleban Islamic militia at the weekend is the latest in a series of successes that transformed once mysterious student vigilantes to virtual masters of war-torn Afghanistan.

The Taleban emerged as a movement of Islamic religious students in the southern province of Kandahar in October 1994. Its rise to power is only the most recent round in almost a quarter century of turmoil.
The following is a chronology of main events in Afghanistan since the end of the monarchy in 1973:
1973 - After more than two centuries of monarchy, King Zahir Shah ousted in a military takeover led by cousin Mohammad Daoud.
1978 - President Daoud killed in leftist coup. Nur Mohammad Taraki elected president of revolutionary council. Islamic groups start armed protests against communist policies.
1979 - Hafizullah Amin appointed prime minister, becomes president after shootout in which Taraki is killed.
1979, December - Soviet transport planes land in Kabul, troops seize key buildings and radio station to install Babrak Karmal as president. Amin executed.

1980 - U.N. General Assembly calls for immediate withdrawal of foreign troops. Afghan guerrilla groups in Pakistan form alliance and start receiving arms from Pakistan, United States, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, China and other backers to fight Soviet troops.
1987 - Karmal replaced by secret police chief Najibullah. Soviet Union begins seeking an end to the war.
1988, April - Pakistan, Afghanistan, the Soviet Union and the United States sign agreement in Geneva for withdrawal of all Soviet troops from Afghanistan by February 15, 1989.

1989, February - Last Soviet soldier departs, leaving Najibullah in power. Exiled Mujahideen consultative council, or shura, elects moderate Sibghatullah Mojadidi executive president and hardliner Abdurrab Rasul Sayyaf prime minister of a "provisional government."

1992, April - Najibullah government falls to Mujahideen. Rival guerrilla groups fight for control of Kabul. Mojadidi enters Kabul and takes over as new head of state. He is replaced within months by Burhanuddin Rabbani.
1993 - Inconclusive fighting between factions led by Ahmad Shah Masood, Gulbuddin Hekmatyar and Rabbani, leaving more than 10,000 civilians dead.
1994 - Factional battles continue between forces loyal to the president and Prime Minister Hekmatyar and his allies, reducing Kabul to rubble and forcing many of its residents to flee the city.
Aug 1994 - A senior mullah from the southern town of Kandahar, Mohammad Omar Akhund, sets up the Taleban, a group of Islamic religious students, who quickly emerge as a powerful guerrilla force.
1995 - Taleban continue their offensive, reaching gates of Kabul in February. They are ousted in March by troops loyal to President Burhanuddin Rabbani in militia's first major defeat.
In October they advance to gates of Kabul for second time, capturing Charasyab and later Rishkor and Khairabad hills.
April - About 1,000 Moslem clergymen choose Taleban leader Mullah Mohammad Omar as Amir-ul-Momineen (commander of the faithful), denouncing Rabbani as unfit to lead Islamic nation.

June - Government confirms loss of Chaghcharan, capital of the central province of Ghor, to Taleban. Taleban launch deadly rocket attack on Kabul, killing at least 54 people and wounding 118, as Hekmatyar resumes post of prime minister under peace deal with Rabbani.

Sept - Taleban launch offensive in eastern Afghanistan, capture Jalalabad, two eastern provinces and then Kabul. They hang Najibullah and his brother Shahpur Ahmadzai and declare Afghanistan a "completely Islamic state". Russia expresses its "grave concern".
Jan 16 - Taleban forces take the Soviet-built Bagram airbase north of Kabul forcing opposition to move further north.
April 21 - Taleban says it has crushed a revolt in some eastern provinces.
May 18 - Taleban forces launch offensive against opposition forces in central Afghanistan.
May 19 - Pro-Taleban mutiny in opposition alliance by ethnic Uzbek General Abdul Malik leads to capture of the northwestern province of Faryab.

May 24 - Taleban and its new allies led by General Malik seize Shibarghan, Dostum's military headquarters and capital of Jozjan province, and Mazar-i-Sharif, Dostum's main stronghold and capital of Balkh province.
May 25 - Taleban sources and an Afghan news service report the capture of the northern provincial capitals of Kunduz and Baghlan and the province of Samangan.
